Welcome to Voat. I'm a new member as well.

Voat has a couple upsides over reddit right now from what I've noticed.

Better Layout

The editting bar for comments is a small feature, but something I definitely appreciate.

The Sets Feature

This is probably my favorite feature. As of right now large subreddits become a pile of loosely collected shit. Lets take /r/dota2 as an example. You get esports news, game updates, art, funny posts, gameplay discussion, and bug reports. With Voat we can have /v/dota2esports, /v/dota2art, /v/dota2official, /v/dota2funny, /v/dota2bugs, /v/dota2discussion and put them in a set named "DotA2." Now you can subscribe to the whole set and browse it at once (as if you were looking at /r/dota2) or you can unsubscribe from any particular subverses you dislike so you get the /r/dota2 you want. It's just ideal.

Unseats 'power users'

It's no secret that a lot of the same people moderate the big subreddits together and it's a real problem because they largely determine what kind of content can be posted on reddit. With a new community a new set of community heads gets to step forth and try their hand. Now it's not guaranteed they'll do any better, but it's more likely than unseating the power users in reddit.

Of course there are issues with this community as well. A lot of the members seem to be rather snobby and entitled and I hope it doesn't effect the community long term.

Well, basically what the title days. My girl was on the playground today climbing up a ladder and a little boy was climbing down at the same time. She says he pushed her, but when I ask her if it was an accident she says she doesn't know. The daycare employee says she didn't see what happened and my daughter had already fallen and was hurt by the time she got over there to see what happened. The cut was really deep and required an emergency room visit and stitches. What do I do now? Do I keep taking her there? Do they need to pay my hospital copay and any bills I get stuck with?
My kid fell and got a huge gash on her head at daycare. Needed stitches. Is daycare liable?

Not a lawyer (and speaking regarding things in the US), but I honestly don't know how much of a case you'd have on this one. The only thing making them remotely liable, and I use that term loosely, is the worker stated she wasn't watching your daughter at the moment the accident happened. Was she watching other kids at the time, or playing Candy Crush on her phone?

Even if she had her eyes on your daughter, from what you've described to us it's debatable whether she could have done anything or not. Short her hovering right behind your daughter I can easily see things playing out the same way no matter how many eyes were on them.

Now, as to whether you keep taking her there, that's up to you. Do kids get hurt there frequently? As @LwnMowerMan said, kids are going to get hurt. How many times do kids get hurt at school for one reason or another? Off the top of my head I can't think of any suits against schools outside of gross negligence.

Now, jumping back to the day care's liability. If you want to try to pursue anything I recommend you start by looking over your enrollment paperwork. They should have something covering injuries somewhere in there. If you're seriously considering taking it farther, you can start there. If what you see appeases you then drop it. If not, you'll want a lawyer at this point.

Again, not a lawyer and not offering legal advice. Just answering your questions as best I can, and outlining what I'd probably be doing if something like that happened to one of my kids.

My kids like the daycare center and haven't been hurt yet. I'm just so mad that the employee didn't know what happened and from what I gathered she didn't try very hard to figure it out. I don't want to press charges but I wish they had to pay my copay!

Well, it sounds like your daughter is still happy with where she's at, which is good. If you don't mind answering, how old is your daughter?

In regards to them not figuring out what happened, I'll present you with two scenarios. One, they barely bothered asking, if that. They got enough details to fill out their report and called it a day. Two, your daughter didn't tell them what she told you. Heaven knows, with my kids at least, I often get half the explanation (if that) on why we're crying like our best friend died, but mommy will get the whole story and then some with less questions.

Each scenario is likely, and you certainly know your daughter better than us, but is it possible she just wasn't telling them for whatever reason? As for the boy, if he did in fact push her like she says he did he could have decided to gloss over that fact to avoid getting in trouble. Couple that with your daughter probably being more focused on the cut on her head and I can easily see the specifics not being revealed at the time of the initial incident report. Again, you know this situation better than us, but is this possible?

Now, as for the copay, they may or may not be able to do anything about that. They likely have insurance to cover things like this, so it's possible that could cover it. Outside of that you might be able to negotiate a discount off of a few weeks of care to make up the difference.

In regards to how hard you push, please keep in mind whether you want to stay with them or not. If you push too hard or ask for too much (though covering the copay as a gesture of good will wouldn't be too much in my book considering how much those places charge) you may not be able to leave your daughter with them anymore. If you become one of those parents they will get it in their heads that they're better off with you not being a customer.

At any rate, hopefully this gets worked out to your satisfaction, or at least to some compromise that you can live with.
